stance_basis: Staff critiques applicant's analysis of coldwater habitat loss and projects elimination of trout habitat under combined project operation
summary: FPC Staff challenges the applicant's characterization of habitat loss in Jocassee Reservoir, arguing that a simple year-to-year comparison understates the cumulative thermal impacts of the Jocassee pumped storage plant operating in conjunction with Lake Keowee. Staff further projects that under full combined operation of the Jocassee and Bad Creek Projects, optimum coldwater trout habitat in the main body of Jocassee Reservoir would be eliminated. Staff's position implies that the project as proposed raises serious unresolved concerns about aquatic habitat impacts.
complaint_summary: Staff argues that the applicant's year-to-year comparison of habitat loss in Jocassee Reservoir inadequately captures the cumulative thermal impact of the Jocassee pumped storage plant removing cool water during generation and discharging warm water during pumping, and that the proposed Bad Creek Project would further accelerate the removal of coldwater habitat.

statement.text: Staff believes that comparing the depth and thickness of habitat loss in Jocassee Reservoir for 1974 and 1975 does not fully explain the effect the operation of the Jocassee pumped storage plant, in conjunction with Lake Keowee, has on the reservoir habitat. The greatest impact on the coldwater layer during the stratified period would be caused by the cumulative effect over 3 to 4 months of the Jocassee Project's removing some cool water during the generating cycle and discharging warm water during the pumping cycle. In addition, the proposed Bad Creek Project would remove some cool water from the Jocassee Reservoir during the pumping cycle and discharge warm water during the generating cycle, thereby accelerating the removal of coldwater habitat.
